items.title: 📱 3.2: the Workshop from a phone
items.body: On an iPhone the Present Characters panel had no way into the Workshop: a long press on a card showed Apple's image sheet instead of the menu, and the little roster button in the panel's header was too small for a finger, so the tap folded the shelf instead. Now a long press on a card (half a second, finger still) opens the card menu where your finger is, and on any touch screen the roster button is a proper button. With a mouse nothing changed. And if the Workshop ever fails to load, a message says so and how to fix it, instead of a tap that does nothing.

items.title: 🎒 3.2: Inventory (beta)
items.body: Settings → Stats → Inventory: a pack for your character and one pouch the party shares, kept per chat. The AI keeps them up to date from a short tag at the end of each reply: what was picked up, handed over, spent or used up (a cigarette smoked, a ration eaten, an arrow loosed counts). A toast says what changed; swiping a reply puts its changes back. The Present Characters panel gets an Inventory page beside Characters, with an editor for anything the AI got wrong, and a Quests page.

items.title: 🗺️ 3.2: Cut to a quest
items.body: Right-click a quest on the panel's Quests page (hold it on a phone) and Cut to it: the story jumps to that quest where the scene stands, with the facts of now carried along.

items.title: ❤️ 3.1.5: vitals off means off
items.body: If you tried Track vitals and switched it off again, the AI was still being shown your characters' Health and the rest from before, and kept updating them, costing tokens every reply with nothing on screen to show for it. The switch now covers what the AI is reminded of as well as what it is asked for: with vitals off, no stats reach the prompt. Nothing in your chats is deleted; switch vitals back on and they start fresh from their starting values.

items.title: 🎲 3.1.5: an NPC's roll finds its sheet
items.body: You set a character's attributes in the Workshop, the game master called for a check on them, and the roll ignored the sheet: the call named them as the scene does ("Mara", "the guard") while the sheet was stored under the card's name ("Mara Vane"), and the dice looked only for the exact name. Now a first or last name, a title around the name, "the guard" for Guard, or any alias from the Workshop finds the sheet, and the roll box names the character as the card does. When two sheets could fit, the one on the shelf wins; when that is still unclear, the roll stays on the default sheet rather than a wrong one. The same goes for saving throws and the dice tool.

items.title: 🛟 3.1.4: hidden means hidden
items.body: Some of you switched Show the Doom button off and the D stayed. 3.1.3 hid it with a stylesheet rule, which a Custom CSS line pinning the D in place, or a second, older copy of the extension loaded beside this one, could outrank. The button now also carries an inline display: none that nothing in a stylesheet outranks, on every Doom button on the page; the switch, /des reset and a reload all apply it. If the D still shows after this update, make the browser fetch the scripts again: hard-reload on a computer (Ctrl+Shift+R); on an iPhone, Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data, remove the site, open it again. A browser (Safari above all), or a CDN in front of a hosted SillyTavern, can keep the old scripts after an update, and DES now tells you when that has happened, with the steps for your device. Then check SillyTavern's Custom CSS for a dooms-settings-fab line and the extensions folder for a second copy.

items.title: 🛟 3.1.3: a way in, always, and a switch for the Doom button
items.body: Settings → Doom Button has a new switch, Show the Doom button, for everyone who asked to hide the floating D. With it off the settings stay reachable from Extensions → Doom's Enhancement Suite → Open Settings and from /des in the chat box. And nothing can lock you out any more: Hide SillyTavern top bar works only while the Doom button shows with Doom's Settings in its fly-out, switching the extension off brings the bar back, a saved combination that would have left no way in is repaired when the page loads, and /des reset puts the bar, the button and the fly-out back from the chat box.

items.title: 🎲 3.1.2 and 3.1.3: a roll result you can change
items.body: With Settings → Stats → Let me change the ruling on, the die number is a button: on the roll box at the top of a reply, and, for rolls the dice tool made, right on the "Tool calls: Dice check" line. Press it and arrows appear either side; each press moves the die one face (20 wraps round to 1) and the total and the outcome follow at once. Press the number again, or click anywhere else, to close, and when the die moved a prompt asks whether to regenerate the reply so the story follows. The box says what the die really showed, and the result the AI is handed is rewritten with it. The game master's own NPC calls at the end of a reply stay as rolled.

items.title: 🩹 3.1.1: Roll a check, readable
items.body: The Roll a check window is solid under every look (the chat used to show through it and fight its text), its Cancel and Discard buttons are plain secondary buttons you can read against the window, and its body scrolls on a short screen so OK is always within reach. The notes below are the beta's.

items.title: 🧪 A beta: nothing changes until you switch something on
items.body: Everything on the new Settings → Stats page is off until you turn it on, so this update changes nothing on screen, and nothing in your prompt beyond the one sentence noted under the tracker below. The Stats features are built and covered by tests, but nobody except their author has played them through yet: that is what the Beta badges mean. When something breaks, Settings → Stats → Report a problem opens a GitHub issue with your DES version, your Stats switches and the last lines of the Notification and System logs already filled in, and copies the full logs to your clipboard for the Logs box. A chat export (the chat menu → Manage chat files → Export) is the single most useful thing to attach.

items.title: ❤️ Vitals
items.body: Settings → Stats → Track vitals. Health, Energy, Satiety, Stamina, Morale, Sanity and Arousal (Hygiene and Mana are ready but off) as 0–100 bars on every portrait card and on the card's back, moved by the AI with each reply and editable with a click on the back. Your persona gets them too. Each vital has a name, colour, icon, starting value and an AI-updated switch; one with AI off keeps its value whatever the AI returns. About a dozen tokens per vital per character per reply. Separate and External modes, per-swipe data, History Persistence and the Tracker Data dropdown all carry them.

items.title: 🎲 Attributes and dice checks
items.body: Settings → Stats → Attributes and dice checks. Every character gets the six D&D attributes (the list is yours to edit) with 5e's skills under each and proficiency ticks, on a Workshop → Attributes tab with Standard array and Roll 4d6 drop lowest to fill a sheet. To make a check, press the d20 by the wand (or Roll a check on your persona's card or in the floating menu), pick an attribute, a skill under it or any skill with any attribute, add a line of context, and OK. When you send, the game master rules the difficulty from your message in one small call, DES rolls the die with real randomness, decides success in code and hands the AI a verdict to narrate. The result sits in a box at the top of the reply, swipes keep it, and once rolled it is final. Scores reach the AI only when a roll rides along, unless you choose Always.

items.title: 🧙 The game master calls for checks
items.body: With attributes on, the game master may call for a check when the story has stakes: as a line at the end of its reply with any model, or through a dice tool where your API supports function calling. A call on you becomes the pending check above the message box (× declines it) and rolls when you send against the difficulty already given; a call on an NPC rolls on that NPC's own sheet the moment the reply renders and is handed to the next reply as a verdict. How often is yours to set (Sparingly, or Whenever an attempt could plausibly fail), each way has its own switch, and Notify on dice events shows a toast at every step so you can see what it is doing.

items.title: 🛡️ Saving throws, tiers and freeform magic
items.body: Saving throws: when one character acts on another, the one acted upon rolls to resist, against a DC built from the actor's own bonus, with a Save tick per attribute in the Workshop; every verdict now says whose roll it is and what success means. Tiers: five tiers from Ordinary to Legend fill an NPC's sheet in one press (Fill by tier), Suggest from the story asks the AI for a sheet from what the chat says about them, and a switch that starts off does that by itself for every new face on the shelf. Casting: magic with no spell list. A Casting chip on INT, WIS or CHA in the Workshop names the ability a character's power runs on, so the game master can ask for a casting check or a target's save, and talents on the sheet (Practised or Master) go to the AI with their bonuses.

items.title: 🗂️ The tracker, in a crowd and after a roll
items.body: The default tracker instructions now ask for every NPC in the scene, including anyone who arrives or speaks in that reply, so a story rule about how many characters feature no longer shrinks the list. If your Tracker Instructions are a custom text, paste that sentence in from the Prompts editor's default. In together mode, a reply that comes without its tracker block now gets one separate request for it, so thoughts and the scene never freeze; a toast says when that happens, Settings → Generation has the switch, Refresh Tracker Data shows in together mode too, and the next generation is reminded to include the block.

items.title: 🔊 Voices
items.body: Steadiness (Settings → Voices → Delivery, off by default) sends a temperature with every line so a designed voice drifts less from line to line, and each line of a designed voice now carries a short anchor drawn from its description. Audition ×3 renders a test line three times back to back so you can hear whether a voice holds. Workshop → Voice has a delivery note for that character, used in place of the global one. Never whisper stops whispered delivery for good. The Voices page is grouped into General, Delivery, Connections and My custom voices, and Connections shows only the key for the service you picked.
